concepts: Risk-neutral integration, GBM exact grid-point sampling and terminal-forward mean.
Sampling SE/CLT intervals versus realized error, model error and grid error.
Euler-Maruyama, full truncation, Heston QE and the Feller boundary.
Philox replay, Box-Muller normals, Sobol context and Kahan reduction.

exercises.original_requirement: Halve error with four times the paths, correctly interpreted.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Sixteen-seed panel compares average SE and realized RMSE; asserts broad average-SE ratio without promising monotone error per seed.

exercises.original_requirement: Break the Feller condition and explain.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Hand Euler negative-variance step plus a finite positive native QE estimate; failure of Feller is not model invalidity.

exercises.original_requirement: Explain weak antithetic gains for symmetric payoffs.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Even z-squared payoff gives identical reflected values; equal raw-path budget loses independent observations and worsens measured SE.

financial_and_api_decisions: EuropeanPricer, PathDependentPricer and LsmcPricer are fixed-GBM helpers; their models field is empty because no registry model key is supplied.
European serial and parallel estimates replay identically with the same seed, grid and inputs.
For one-step LsmcPricer antithetics, num_paths=N counts independent pair means and num_simulated_paths=2N counts generated trajectories. Compare with 2N plain samples at the same raw-path budget.
The captured GBM helper includes the initial state; it does not expose engine or scheme injection.
Four times as many independent samples halves the theoretical standard-error scale, not the realized absolute error of every seed.
The source set also includes stochastic_processes, discretization_schemes and monte_carlo_simulation; the principal notebook identifies the replay proof.

scope: Full original per-lesson plan and companion syllabus; every original exercise group required.
concepts: Arithmetic versus geometric Asian averages and fixing conventions; exact one-fixing identity.
Kemna-Vorst geometric control-variate context and Turnbull-Wakeman approximation.
Nested discrete barrier monitoring, continuous Reiner-Rubinstein benchmark and BGK correction context.
Longstaff-Schwartz backward regression, exercise-grid error, basis variance and independent policy evaluation.
Native co-terminal Hull-White tree and Monte Carlo Bermudan swaption pricing.
Discrete lookback dominance, regression overfit diagnostics and quanto FX-quote/correlation convention.
Computed spot-versus-held-out-policy/European/intrinsic plots; explicitly prescribed non-engine policy schematic; executable 256/1024/4096-pair study with two independent pricing seeds.

exercises.original_requirement: Show lookback payoff at least as large as matched vanilla.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Same captured paths, pathwise maximum-versus-terminal inequality and vanilla Black-Scholes four-SE check.

exercises.original_requirement: Demonstrate overfit foresight bias with too few paths and high degree.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Eight-seed panel compares training and held-out values for degree one and six with 96 training paths.

exercises.original_requirement: Price quanto and identify its required correlation.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Native correlation sweep with domestic-per-foreign FX quote; zero-correlation/equal-rates vanilla identity.

financial_and_api_decisions: asian_option_price with arithmetic averaging is the Turnbull-Wakeman approximation; geometric averaging uses the exact benchmark. One terminal fixing reduces both to the matched European contract.
barrier_call prices continuous monitoring and accepts no monitoring-frequency parameter. The discrete sweep uses nested observations on the same captured fine paths.
price_american_put_unbiased evaluates a fitted exercise policy on independent pricing paths. Its Monte Carlo interval does not include exercise-grid or learned-policy error.

No exercise-boundary object is exposed by LsmcPricer. A clearly labelled prescribed schematic is independent of engine output; actual spot-price and path-count plots report held-out policy values with sampling bars and explicit policy/grid-error limits.

Fixed-strike lookback is computed directly on captured GBM paths and dominates the matched terminal vanilla payoff path by path. The continuous fixed-strike helper is deliberately excluded: its M>=K branch calls the floating-strike formula, creating a discontinuity at K=M (17.216802 at K=100 versus 19.167624 at K=100.000001 for S=M=100, r=5%, q=0, sigma=20%, T=1). No analytical accuracy claim is made for the substituted discrete payoff.

quanto_option_price is validated by a correlation sweep with domestic-currency-per-foreign FX quotation and unit contractual conversion: effective foreign-equity drift r_f-q-rho*sigma_s*sigma_fx; equal domestic/foreign rates with rho=0 reduce to the vanilla formula.

The mapped exotic_rates notebook prices an explicitly configured co-terminal Bermudan with both registered Hull-White 1F tree and Monte Carlo models. Seed replay, path count, finite standard error and a fixture-specific cross-method tolerance execute. The default LSMC diagnostic is not a held-out policy-error bound; this registered wrapper does not expose the independent pricing_seed argument of the standalone GBM helper.

scope: Full original per-lesson plan and companion syllabus; every original exercise group required.
concepts: Structured-note redemption, short knock-in put, coupon targets/recursions/range observation arithmetic.
Actual positive pool assets; cash waterfall, OC/IC trigger context, prepayment/default/severity/recovery timing.
Different capital-stack versus loss-attachment coordinates.
One-factor Gaussian conditional PD, Vasicek granular limit and finite-pool Monte Carlo loss allocation.
Factor-copula semi-analytic context, base-correlation bootstrap procedure and actual curve repricing.
PV/price/WAL/OAS, floating-only discount margin and first-writedown CDR.
Conditional correlation signs and the Gaussian dependence, recovery, calibration and liquidity limitations.

exercises.original_requirement: Equity versus senior value response to correlation.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Fixed-PD/LGD loss-only expected principal has opposite signs; explanation separates that experiment from universal traded-price claims.

exercises.original_requirement: Read breakeven CDR from the scenario table.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Grid brackets first writedown between 1% and 2%, native solve near 1.7258%, model-price OAS near zero and fixed-coupon discount-margin rejection.

exercises.original_requirement: Explain Gaussian copula assumptions in a crisis.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Complete disclosure solution addresses tail dependence, changing PD/recovery dependence, calibration non-identification, surface arbitrage, structural cash flows and liquidity.

financial_and_api_decisions: The supported JSON instrument type is autocallable, dispatched through its registered GBM model. All observed fixings are supplied, so this proof takes the deterministic known-redemption branch.
Zero coupons, unreachable autocall barriers and a zero discount rate isolate the final capital-protection, participation and knock-in-put redemption contracts.
The note holder is short the knock-in put: principal is reduced by the put loss after breach. A breach followed by full spot recovery returns principal.
This proof is a payoff-contract identity, not an issuer-credit or new-issue valuation model.

StructuredCredit requires actual positive PoolAssets for pricing; metadata-only rep lines are not a substitute. The separate track fixture tests supply the pool, waterfall and base-correlation evidence.

The mapped exotic_rates notebook hand-reconciles the TARN target and truncated final coupon, snowball recursion, inverse-floater gearing, and an inclusive range-accrual observation fraction. These are coupon-profile arithmetic helpers, not complete callable-note or issuer-credit valuation models.
The two-asset cashflow waterfall now directly reconciles all three native tranche PVs to one-period receipts, with real positive PoolAssets.
Finite-pool Gaussian exposures use sqrt(asset correlation) loadings. Expected pool loss is PD times LGD times notional; exact pathwise loss tranches reconcile to native tranche statistics.
The native breakeven CDR is the first-writedown threshold, not a par-price target. OAS reprices model price to approximately zero spread; fixed-coupon discount margin is explicitly rejected.
Cash-stack attachment coordinates differ from the loss-only tranche coordinates used by PortfolioLossResult. Base-correlation knots are detachment percentage points; correlations are decimals.

scope: Full original per-lesson plan and companion syllabus; every original exercise group required.
concepts: R-7 empirical return quantile, sign/horizon units and closed-threshold ES estimator.
Exact tail-probability ES definition, VaR non-subadditivity and tied-data limitation.
Gaussian and Cornish-Fisher tails on a controlled skewed sample, moment instability.
Benchmark beta and aligned unrestricted OLS: intercept, coefficients, R-squared and residual orthogonality.

Ledoit-Wolf covariance shrinkage and explicitly dimensioned systematic dollar risk.
Credit hierarchy, calibration persistence, decimal input spreads/basis-point output, DTS weights and annualized covariance.

exercises.original_requirement: Convert 95% one-day risk to 99% ten-day risk under explicit assumptions.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Native Gaussian horizon quantile matches drift-plus-z99 formula within 1e-9; wrong 95% square-root shortcut differs.

financial_and_api_decisions: 504 aligned synthetic daily proxy returns are not an actual historical mark series for the common priced book.

Historical VaR uses R-7 interpolation; historical expected_shortfall includes every observation at or below the threshold. The displayed exact-tail-mass ES proof handles ties separately before invoking coherence.
Multi-factor OLS is unrestricted, uses already-excess factors and zero risk-free return in this fixture; residual orthogonality, R-squared and benchmark beta are checked against NumPy references.
CreditCalibrator takes decimal spreads; the calibrated spread-decomposition outputs are in basis points. DTS calibration supplies explicit spread durations.

The stored credit covariance is annualized; OneStep exposes that covariance and NSteps(12) literally multiplies it by twelve. Illustrative USD 1000 per native factor-unit exposures cover systematic risk only.
neutralize_and_zscore uses population standard deviation; the exercise asserts mean zero, exposure orthogonality and population variance one.

scope: Full original per-lesson plan and companion syllabus; every original exercise group required.

Quarterly-to-annual terminal flow, Gordon denominator, terminal dominance and short-forecast limitations.

exercises.original_requirement: Reconcile exit-multiple and Gordon terminal value.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: Derive implied 7.9264x multiple from Gordon TV and annualized EBITDA, reprice through native exit-multiple method to one cent.

exercises.original_requirement: Turn revenue-growth Monte Carlo into an EV distribution.
exercises.solution_and_assertions: 1024 retained joint native statement paths individually repriced through native DCF; no stitching marginal percentiles.

financial_and_api_decisions: The native shared borrower operating graph supplies UFCF; USD is stamped at the monetary DCF boundary and all original actuals and baseline UFCF values are preserved.
WACC is 9.76875%; terminal flow is the annual trailing-four-quarter sum. Approximately 93.16% of EV is terminal PV, so this short teaching horizon is assumption-sensitive.
A native DCF grid and DcfSensitivityResult measure value effects; the separate operating tornado measures one-quarter UFCF and is labelled separately.
ScenarioSet changes forecast driver levels only; every native scenario UFCF path is repriced through evaluate_dcf, preserving the base result.
The bounded native goal_seek changes only perpetual terminal growth and is validated by a native DCF reprice against the market-equity target.

Native LBO sources/uses, debt roll-forward, after-tax cash feasibility and an independent equity-profit bridge are checked. All cash is reserved for operating liquidity, with no interim distributions or excess-cash credit; entry latest-actual EBITDA is explicitly pinned because evaluate_lbo reads the first model period.

ForecastSpec.log_normal and Evaluator.evaluate_monte_carlo are the supported APIs. Retained joint quarterly UFCF paths are individually repriced by native DCF; marginal percentiles are never stitched into a fake path.
